$note: A REWRITE pivot: this model's candidates for one variable across the cells it wrote, each beside the original and its gate result. Truth is Reading/Database/templates/by_variable (generated from by_axis).

candidate.text: You see what a thing will become before it looks like anything. Needing a way forward is how you feel safe, and that puts the far chance ahead of the near one. Trust that early sight, and keep track of what is already yours.

angles.drive: Reading the real value of things is your standing talent, and it works on houses, people, and offers alike. You see the water damage behind the fresh paint and the good bones behind the ugly listing. Bad deals rarely survive your first slow walk around them.
angles.cost_self: Everyone else toured the staged interior. You spent nine minutes in the basement with a flashlight and offered twelve percent under asking, with reasons attached. The sellers argued, then folded. Two years later the neighbors are still asking how you got that price.
angles.cost_others: Friends bring you their contracts the way people bring jewelry to an appraiser. You flip straight to the page where deals go wrong, and you are rarely wrong about which page that is. Your fee is a coffee, and the savings have bought several people cars.

candidate.text: Waiting for a better chance has never been your way. Being in motion steadies you, and it puts the chance you can take today ahead of any promised for later. Take it, and know that moving early means paying for a few that go nowhere.

angles.drive: Ground you have personally covered is your actual education. Markets, cities, kitchens, border towns: you learn places by standing in them, and every trip quietly becomes inventory. When a decision needs context, you usually have some, bought at the price of having been there.
angles.cost_self: The supplier problem stumped the office for a week, and you solved it with one call to a man you met at a trade fair in 2021, in a city nobody else could place. The office called it luck. Your contact list calls it coverage.
angles.cost_others: People assume your stories are exaggerated until they travel with you once and watch three strangers in two cities greet you by name. The network was not built at desks. It was built at long tables, and it keeps paying for itself in favors.

candidate.text: Sharing what you win comes more naturally to you than banking it. A win that stays with you feels unfinished, and that puts giving it away ahead of keeping it. Share it, and count what is missing from the bank as a price you chose.

angles.drive: Plenty follows you around, and you spread it without doing the math. The garden overproduces, the table seats extras, the referral goes out before being asked for. Abundance is your operating assumption, and somehow the assumption keeps proving itself right.
angles.cost_self: You came back from the weekend market with too much of everything, again, and by Sunday night four households had bags on their porches. Nobody keeps score, least of all you. Somehow your own porch is never empty either, which you have stopped calling coincidence.
angles.cost_others: Around you, people relax about money in a way they cannot explain. There is always somehow enough, and some extra, and a plan for the extra. Scarcity thinking finds no soil at your table, and guests leave having borrowed a little of your assumption.

candidate.text: Whatever you own, you keep working for years. Buying new feels like giving up on something, and that puts fixing ahead of replacing every time. Keep making things last, and let a few of them go while they still have worth to someone.

angles.drive: Getting full value out of things is a craft you practice daily and almost invisibly. The repaired instead of replaced, the bought-once-properly, the leftovers built into a second dinner. Waste offends you mildly and constantly, and your accounts show what mild constant offense saves.
angles.cost_self: The winter coat is on its ninth season, re-zipped twice by the tailor whose name you know. Colleagues in this year’s jackets tease you about it. The retirement account you never mention could quietly buy everyone at the table a coat store.
angles.cost_others: Nobody watched you be careful, and everyone sees what the care built. The coat is nine seasons old and the house is paid for, a math the flashy spenders around you have slowly started doing out loud. You never once explained it. The results explain it, late and completely.

candidate.text: Money feels like yours only after part of it is put away. Being covered matters more to you than being treated, and the saving comes before the spending. Keep that order, and spend one saved thing on yourself from time to time.

angles.drive: Holding course is your competitive advantage in a distractible world. The plan from January is still the plan in September, adjusted, funded, on schedule. Shiny alternatives pitch themselves at you weekly and bounce off politely. What you committed to, you finish.
angles.cost_self: While the group chat cycled through four investment fads in a year, your boring monthly transfer went through forty-eight times, unphotographed. Two of the fads ended badly for people you love. Your account did the thing accounts are supposed to do, quietly, again.
angles.cost_others: People set their watches by your consistency and occasionally roll their eyes at it, until their own zigzags total up. Then they come asking about the boring transfer. You show them the math, kindly, without once saying the sentence you have earned.

candidate.text: Loyalty is your default, given before it is asked for. Choosing again asks less of you than starting fresh, and that puts the person you have ahead of anyone new. Keep giving it, and let the few people you never met be the price.

angles.drive: Reserves are your love language and your strategy. The pantry, the savings, the spare parts drawer, the contact who owes you one: whatever the situation needs, some corner of your life already holds it. Emergencies visit you and find the door already answered.
angles.cost_self: During the outage, your house was the one with candles, a charged power bank, cash, and cocoa. Three neighbors ended up in your kitchen playing cards by lamplight. It was, one of them said, the nicest blackout of their life. You had planned for worse.
angles.cost_others: People tease you about the stockpiles until the day they call you from a breakdown lane, a storm, or a sudden expense. You always have the thing. Around you, disasters get downgraded to inconveniences, and nobody fully registers who did the downgrading.

candidate.text: Going first is how you find out if a thing is real. Being bold costs less than being left behind, and you go ahead of knowing where you land. You spend yourself going first, and one turn handed away gives some of it back.

angles.drive: Upward is your body’s default direction, and speed is its signature. New job, new ladder, new wall: you find the holds faster than anyone expects, and you are halfway up before the group finishes stretching. Height that takes others years takes you seasons.
angles.cost_self: You joined in March as the junior hire and by December were running the standup, through momentum rather than coup. The org chart caught up to reality in the spring. Somebody checked the dates twice, assuming a typo. The dates were right.
angles.cost_others: Peers track your ascent with a mix of inspiration and vertigo. Some train harder because you exist, which you would take as the highest compliment. The ones who resent it are mostly resenting the mirror. You climb past both kinds without slowing.

candidate.text: Whenever a race starts near you, you find new speed. Being compared reads as a reason, and you chase another's lead instead of starting from nothing. You love the race more than the finish, and letting one go costs you nothing you would miss.

angles.drive: Nerve is your renewable resource. You ask for the number with a straight face, take the shot with the game on the line, sign up before feeling ready. Fear shows up on schedule and finds you already moving, which it never quite gets used to.
angles.cost_self: You asked for forty percent above the posted range, out loud, in the actual meeting, while your co-applicants asked for the midpoint. The pause lasted four seconds. You got thirty-two percent and a reputation. Both are still compounding.
angles.cost_others: People borrow your nerve for their own risky moments, asking what you would do and then, crucially, whether you would come along. You usually would. Half your circle’s boldest stories feature you standing just off-camera, having dared them into the frame.

candidate.text: Sharing the risk is the first thing you offer. You like a bet best with someone else's name beside yours, because carrying it alone turns daring into worry. You split the risk ahead of measuring it, and measuring first keeps the friendship whole.

angles.drive: Competition is your fertilizer. A rival in the field and your growth doubles: the training sharpens, the hours deepen, the work finds another gear you did not know the engine had. You do not resent your rivals. You privately thank them, at the finish line.
angles.cost_self: The gym was dying at six in the morning until the newcomer started matching your pace. Within a month you were both twenty percent stronger and nodding like diplomats. Neither of you has ever named the arrangement. Both of you check the other’s numbers first.
angles.cost_others: Coaches and managers quietly use you as the pace car, placing you near whoever needs pushing. It works every time. The people you pull upward mostly like you, once they recover, and the record boards in several places carry the results of arguments you started.

candidate.text: Where help is offered, you do it alone anyway. Needing nothing is a quiet pride, so you do it yourself ahead of leaning on a peer. Accept one offer a month, since doing everything alone costs you every favour you turn away.

angles.drive: Your footing is your own, grown from your own choices and watered on your own schedule. Approval is pleasant weather rather than required rainfall. People with shallower systems topple in seasons you barely notice, and they notice you not noticing.
angles.cost_self: When the industry rumor cycle hit, half your peers rewrote their profiles within a week. You changed nothing, on the grounds that nothing about you had changed. The cycle passed. Your unchanged profile now reads as the confident one, which it always was.
angles.cost_others: People ask your opinion specifically because it was not assembled from the group’s. Your yes means yes and arrives unsponsored. In shifting alliances you are the fixed survey point, and both sides check their positions against yours without telling each other.

candidate.text: You set your own pace and keep it, fast day or slow. Steadiness is what you trust most, and you would sooner arrive late at your speed than early at another's. You reach a few chances late and take the rest at your own pace.

angles.drive: You stand on your own structure, without leaning on charm, on apology, or on anyone’s shoulder. What holds you up is internal, built, and paid for, which is why pressure does not change your shape. People can push. Nothing in you is borrowed enough to come loose.
angles.cost_self: When the funding fell through, three co-founders started calling advisors, mentors, parents. You recalculated your own runway at the kitchen table and adjusted your own plan by morning. Help was offered twice. You took the version that let you stay vertical: information, without the arm.
angles.cost_others: Nobody manages you, worries about you, or checks your footing, and after a while they stop trying to. You lean on no one so consistently that leaning on you feels safe. Half the group’s stability, on inspection, is people steadying themselves against your unborrowed posture.

candidate.text: Whatever the company, you hold the same standard. Being a single person everywhere lets you trust yourself, because a self that bends cannot be measured. You keep your shape rather than borrow a looser one and pay in the ease of blending in.

angles.drive: Continuing is your quiet superpower. Where motivation fails, you simply proceed: the run in the rain, the chapter after a rejection, year six of the practice everyone else left in year one. Time works for you because you never fire it.
angles.cost_self: The Tuesday run has survived four winters, two jobs, and one broken toe, adjusted but never skipped. This morning it was raining sideways and you went anyway, same route, same distance. Nothing about it is impressive on any single day. The years are the unit.
angles.cost_others: Your persistence reads as unremarkable up close, day by day, and staggering in summary. People introduce you with numbers: fifteen years running, four hundred consecutive weeks. The numbers embarrass you slightly. They are also, everyone agrees, the whole explanation.

candidate.text: You go deep or not at all. A subject has to hold you before it gives anything back, so you would rather know one field deep than ten wide. Keep bringing something up, because the way down was only ever yours.

angles.drive: Your mind goes down where others skim across. A subject catches you and you vanish into it for weeks, surfacing with pearls nobody knew were down there. The depth is the method: what you understand, you understand from the floor up.
angles.cost_self: The two-hour documentary became a four-month descent through library loans, forum archives, and one email exchange with a retired professor in Finland. When you finally explained it at dinner, simply and completely, the family sat quiet. The dive had reached the bottom of something.
angles.cost_others: People ask you questions the way they lower buckets into wells, knowing the answer will come up cold and clear and from further down than expected. Experts double-check their own fields after talking to you. Nobody can tell where you find the time. The time is underwater.

candidate.text: You read the gap in a conversation sooner than the words. Sensing the shape underneath keeps you safe, and you act on that shape rather than wait for it to be named. Ask for the words anyway, since an unchecked reading stays a guess.

angles.drive: You sense turns before they announce themselves. The market mood, the friendship cooling, the industry current reversing: something in you registers the shift while the surface still looks calm. You rarely explain the read, because the read arrives without paperwork.
angles.cost_self: You moved your savings in September, citing a feeling with no citation. In November the sector everyone loved gave back three years of gains. Your brother-in-law asked how you knew. You said the water felt different, which was true and did not help him.
angles.cost_others: People have learned to note your quiet exits: from stocks, from projects, from certain gatherings. The reasons surface months later wearing headlines. Being early looks like luck each individual time. Across twenty years it looks like an instrument nobody else was issued.

candidate.text: The things you know best, you taught yourself. Being told never stuck the way your own trying did, and you would rather work a thing out than be shown. You pay for it in the steps you can never show anyone.

angles.drive: Your influence works below the surface, in word choices and timing rather than announcements. You adjust one sentence in the proposal, one name on the invite list, one pause in the conversation, and outcomes shift downstream. Watching for your fingerprints is pointless. Water does not leave any.
angles.cost_self: The reconciliation between your two feuding friends took place, they believe, by accident, at a dinner that happened to include both, seated apart, near topics that happened to soften them. The accident took you three weeks to arrange. Neither has ever suspected a current.
angles.cost_others: People experience your presence as things going strangely smoothly. Meetings you attend reach agreement sooner, disputes near you lose their heat, and nobody can attribute any of it. Credit slides off you like rain, which is how you prefer it. The results stay.

candidate.text: Around you, a hard day gets quieter, and you never point it out. Holding steady for someone comes easier to you than being held yourself, and the calm is real either way. Keep some of it back, because you steady everyone ahead of yourself.

angles.drive: You restore people by being the place where nothing is asked of them. The advice waits until requested, the clock stays out of it, and the visit can be silent without being strange. Their levels rise in your company because your company charges nothing. The mechanism is shelter.
angles.cost_self: Your brother let himself in with the spare key, sat in your kitchen for two hours, and said almost nothing. You read nearby and refilled his glass once. He left standing straighter. The visit will never be mentioned, which is exactly why it worked.
angles.cost_others: People route their worst weeks through your place: the call made from your driveway before going home, the couch that has caught every crisis since 2015. Nobody plans it out loud. The harbor is simply known, the way water is known to be downhill.

candidate.text: What you know, you mostly soaked up rather than looked up. Being around a thing teaches you more than a course on it, and the understanding arrives whole instead of in steps. Let that be enough, because you owe nobody the steps you never took.

angles.drive: Your calm is deep water, not thin ice. Provocations sink into it and are absorbed, deadlines land softly on it, and chaos arrives to find no surface tension to grab. It is not detachment. Everything registers. It just registers into stillness instead of splash.
angles.cost_self: The kitchen caught fire, briefly, at the family gathering, and your voice never left its usual register: pan lid, baking soda, window, done. The story afterward was all about the flames. You remember it as a Tuesday.
angles.cost_others: Storms wear themselves out on you without your doing anything. The furious arrive, talk, slow down, and leave merely tired, their weather absorbed into something deeper than it was. You never argue anyone calm. They pour it in, and the water takes it.

candidate.text: Where a push would be obvious, you stay patient. What arrives in its own time means more to you than what you chased, and you let plans and people come. Keep waiting where it works, and learn the few places where it is only delay.

angles.drive: You take things in fully before responding, which has become rare enough to feel like a gift. The half-formed idea, the clumsy confession, the criticism with truth in it: all get received whole, unjudged on arrival, given somewhere calm to finish becoming what they meant.
angles.cost_self: Your friend rehearsed the coming-out speech for weeks, and your entire response was to refill their glass and ask how long they had known. The speech had prepared for weather. Your table offered none, and the rest of the evening was just dinner, which was everything.
angles.cost_others: People tell you things they have told no one, over ordinary kitchen tables, at ordinary volumes, startled to hear themselves. The secret is that nothing bounces off you. Whatever arrives is received at depth, held without ripples, and everyone somehow knows this before they test it.

candidate.text: Speaking up costs you less than staying quiet does. You carry an unsaid thing like a weight, and saying it comes sooner than wishing you had. Say it anyway, and mind the price, that you spend goodwill faster than you earn it.

angles.drive: When you switch on, everyone else becomes background lighting. The presentation, the toast, the argument you decide to win in style: your output has wattage that cannot be taught, and attention finds you the way moths find porch lights, reliably and a little helplessly.
angles.cost_self: You took the graveyard slot at the conference, the one after lunch on the last day, and by minute six people were texting colleagues to come in. The recording circulated for months. The organizers moved you to the keynote the following year, apologizing for the delay.
angles.cost_others: People plan events partly around whether you will be on form, because your form changes the evening’s category. The risk is known and priced in: you might outshine the occasion itself. Twice now, the couple’s wedding is mostly remembered for your toast. They quote it fondly, mostly.

candidate.text: Performing comes to you more naturally than anything else. You come alive with people watching, and that puts the show ahead of the rehearsal every time. Keep performing, and take the price with it, that you feel most real when watched.

angles.drive: Your mind moves at spark speed. The comeback arrives while the setup is still landing, the solution mid-question, the joke exactly on the beat. In fast company you are the fastest thing present, and slow company speeds up around you out of self-respect.
angles.cost_self: The client’s curveball question, the one designed to embarrass, got an answer so fast and clean that the questioner laughed and wrote it down. Your team debriefed the moment for a week. You could not remember composing the reply. It had simply been lit and ready.
angles.cost_others: People stop mid-story around you to say do not steal this, knowing your version will be funnier by dinner. Writers in your circle keep notes on things you said in passing. At least one printed mug exists. You signed it, obviously, since the line was yours.

candidate.text: Thinking fast is your natural speed. You trust a quick answer more than a considered one, and you prefer nearly right now to fully right later. Keep the speed, with an eye on the cost, that you are sometimes only quick.

angles.drive: At full intensity you do in hours what committees do in quarters. The deadline crunch, the final rehearsal, the last mile: your heat concentrates into something close to alarming, and the output comes back changed from the inside out. Nobody asks what it costs. It visibly costs.
angles.cost_self: The pitch was due at nine and dead at midnight, so you burned from midnight to six and delivered something that made the original plan look like a rough draft of your rough draft. The client signed by lunch. You slept through the celebration, honorably.
angles.cost_others: Colleagues describe your peak state with fire-safety vocabulary, half joking. When you lock in, people clear the area and route materials toward you, knowing the window is real and finite. What comes out of those windows has won accounts, contests, and one national award. Handle accordingly.

candidate.text: You give before anyone asks, and it never feels like spending. Giving is how you know you belong somewhere, and you hand things out ahead of keeping them for yourself. Stay this open-handed, with one eye on how rarely you learn what you wanted.

angles.drive: Your enjoyment broadcasts. The good meal, the small win, the Tuesday sunset: whatever you savor gets amplified through you and lands on everyone nearby, brightening the whole table by contact. Joy in your hands is not private property. It is a utility, and you run the grid.
angles.cost_self: You liked the street musician, so the whole group stopped, and because the group stopped, a crowd formed, and because you clapped like that, others did, and the musician had her best hour of the year. She thanked you specifically. You had simply enjoyed her loudly.
angles.cost_others: Event planners and grandmothers agree on you: seat that one centrally. Your delight is the yeast of gatherings, invisible in the recipe and responsible for the rise. Parties you miss get described afterward with a slight shrug: it was nice. Nice is the word for your absence.

candidate.text: You enjoy things out loud, and the enjoyment spreads. You count a good moment unfinished until someone else is in it, so you share a pleasure sooner than you savor it. Let it spread, with one pleasure kept for yourself all the same.

angles.drive: You find the celebration inside ordinary days and switch it on. The exam passed becomes a dinner, the Friday becomes an occasion, the occasion gets candles. Ritual joy is your craft: you know that marking a moment is what makes it a moment, and you mark relentlessly.
angles.cost_self: The divorce papers were finalized on a Thursday, and by Saturday you had organized, of all things, a party, the exactly right kind, for your friend who needed her new chapter to begin with cake instead of silence. She keeps the photo from that night on her fridge.
angles.cost_others: Your calendar quietly anchors the year for a surprising number of people: the solstice dinner, the first-snow cocoa, the anniversary of nothing in particular. Traditions you invented as jokes now have attendance records. People plan around them, and around you, the way towns plan around festivals.

candidate.text: Things come easily to you, and you let them. Forcing a thing spoils it in your hands, so you wait for the easy way in rather than push at the hard one. Keep that lightness, and know it hides how much you do.

angles.drive: What you express goes straight to the chest. The toast that gets the region misty, the text that arrives on the exactly wrong day and makes it right, the compliment specific enough to keep: your warmth has aim. People store what you say to them, sometimes for decades.
angles.cost_self: At the funeral, your two minutes about the deceased’s terrible parking and enormous heart did what the eulogy could not: the family laughed, then wept, then thanked you at the door, gripping your hand a beat long. The widow quotes your lines now as her own memory.
angles.cost_others: People hand you the emotional assignments nobody else can carry: the toast, the goodbye card everyone signs after you set the tone, the call to the friend in the hospital. Your words reliably reach the part of people that formal language misses. It is a talent disguised as niceness.

candidate.text: You take charge the moment something starts going wrong. Being in charge gives your push a direction, and you reach for it ahead of comfort every time. Let the calm after count too, because every charge you take costs you some rest.

angles.drive: Readiness is your resting state. The plan B exists before plan A launches, the difficult conversation is pre-rehearsed, the go-bag, literal or mental, stays packed. When trouble finally arrives it finds you already dressed, and the calm of the prepared is your signature entrance.
angles.cost_self: The client called at seven with the emergency everyone else needed a day to process, and you opened the folder you had built for exactly this scenario three months earlier, unasked. The call lasted eleven minutes. The folder had been waiting longer than the emergency had existed.
angles.cost_others: People check your reaction before deciding how scared to be, and your reaction is usually to start executing. Teams describe going into hard weeks behind you the way soldiers describe good sergeants: nobody promises it will be pleasant, everybody knows the plan will hold.

candidate.text: You thrive under pressure the way others thrive on praise. Pressure shapes your force, and that is why you take the harder task ahead of the easy one. Enjoy that, and know an easy season with no pressure feels like a loss.

angles.drive: Your discipline is structural steel, not decoration. The habit holds on the bad days, which is the only measurement that counts: the routine survives travel, illness, and success, each of which kills most people’s systems. What you commit to becomes load-bearing, permanently.
angles.cost_self: Two hundred consecutive weeks of the same training schedule, through two job changes and one broken hand, adjusted around the cast rather than paused for it. The physical therapist asked to see the log, then photographed it for her office wall, as evidence of a species.
angles.cost_others: Your consistency reads as almost mechanical until people need to borrow it. Then they discover the practical magic: things placed in your keeping happen, on schedule, indefinitely. Whole projects get architected around your reliability the way bridges get designed around their strongest member.

candidate.text: You decide fast because being wrong sits easier with you than waiting. Metal runs short in you, and one firm decision gives your push the shape it was missing. Trust that, and let the full picture catch up before the next decision.

angles.drive: Your interventions are exact. Where others swing wide, you find the one line to cut, the one word to change, the one person to call, and the problem separates cleanly from the situation. Minimal force, placed precisely: it looks effortless and is actually aim.
angles.cost_self: The failing project had eleven proposed fixes on the whiteboard, and you crossed out ten, changed one contract clause, and the entire dispute dissolved by Friday. The team spent the sprint braced for surgery. What happened was closer to acupuncture, and nobody bled.
angles.cost_others: People bring you tangles the way patients bring specialists their worst scans, hoping for precision instead of sympathy, and receiving exactly that. Your fixes rarely need revisiting. The scar tissue around problems you have handled is famously minimal, which is why the referrals never stop.

candidate.text: You keep your word because a promise is the one rule you wrote. A given word is the firmest shape your plans have, and you honour it ahead of your own comfort. Keep doing that, and notice what your word costs you in evenings.

angles.drive: Exactness is your dialect. The estimate lands within percent, the summary contains nothing loose, the drawer holds what its label claims. Around you, vagueness feels briefly embarrassed of itself, and work passing through your hands comes out true to measure, every time it matters.
angles.cost_self: The budget you built in January closed the year eleven dollars off, across forty accounts, a variance your auditor circled with an exclamation mark and showed to colleagues. You considered the eleven dollars a miss. The auditor considered framing it. Both reactions were, in their way, accurate.
angles.cost_others: People stop estimating around you and start measuring, pulled upward by your example. Documents you have touched become the reference copies. When two versions of any number circulate, meetings resolve the dispute with four words, said without irony: check what theirs says.

candidate.text: You do it properly because half-done never stops bothering you. A standard properly met is the closest you come to rest, and you finish the form ahead of the fun. Keep the standard, and give the fun one proper form of its own.

angles.drive: Your price does not exist. The convenient blindness, the adjusted figure, the favor with strings: each has approached you dressed in reasonable clothes, and each has left unbought. People stopped offering years ago, which is the cleanest audit result a character can post.
angles.cost_self: The developer’s envelope, offered with practiced lightness at the site meeting, was returned across the table before it finished landing, without commentary, and the inspection proceeded to its correct conclusion. The story circulated in both industries. Your approvals, consequently, are bankable at face value, everywhere.
angles.cost_others: Institutions position you where temptation concentrates, treasurer, examiner, referee, because your presence retires a whole category of risk. The compliment is structural: systems relax around your name. Somewhere in three organizations, rules exist that were written shorter because you would be the one holding them.

candidate.text: You earn your place because a title given free would never feel like yours. Earned proof is the only rank you believe in, and you work for it sooner than you ask for it. Enjoy the earning, and ask for it every so often.

angles.drive: Your fairness holds under load. The friend and the stranger get the same terms, the popular opinion and the correct one get separated calmly, and both sides of any dispute leave your table feeling accurately weighed. Balance like yours is engineered. People rest whole arguments on it.
angles.cost_self: The inheritance dispute that was fracturing the family got handed, by unspoken consensus, to you, and your allocation, explained line by line at the kitchen table, was accepted by all four siblings, including the two who arrived with lawyers’ letters. The letters went home unopened.
angles.cost_others: Warring parties agree on you when they can agree on nothing else, which has become its own career. Your rulings hold without enforcement because both sides watched the scales the whole time. The nickname that follows you between organizations translates, roughly, to: the one they both trusted.
